subject: Transportation Systems
title: Navigating by the Stars
description: A quick win: understand Navigating by the Stars.

hook.text: For thousands of years, the night sky was the only reliable map available to travelers and sailors.

buildup.text: Polaris—the North Star—barely moves in the sky. Its height above the horizon tells you your latitude.

discovery.text: Polynesian navigators memorized the rising and setting points of over 200 stars. They needed no instruments.

twist.text: Stars only work on clear nights. Clouds, fog, and light pollution made celestial navigation unreliable at times.

climax.text: Despite limitations, star navigation guided humanity across every ocean long before any instrument existed.

punchline.text: The first GPS was the sky.

quiz.question: How does Polaris help determine a navigator's position?
options: Its height above the horizon indicates latitude
